source_selection.exact_source_expression: When God says 'I AM WHO I AM,' He is not giving a label like other names. He is saying He cannot be defined by anything deeper or larger—He is the root, not a thing among things.
source_selection.reason: The claim has a clear logical structure: a self-naming entity that is not definable by anything deeper or larger, i.e., not a member of a larger category and not explained by something more fundamental. This can be modeled as a formal property of a naming relation and a grounding/explanation relation.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A divine name is 'root-naming' if it does not place the named entity inside a larger category and does not ground the entity's existence in anything deeper. Formally: for an entity g, a name N, and a grounding relation G, N is root-naming for g iff there is no x such that G(x, g) and no category C such that g ∈ C and C is more ultimate than g.

symbol_table.formal_definition: A predicate on names and entities: RootNaming(N, g) iff ¬∃x. G(x, g) ∧ ¬∃C. g ∈ C ∧ MoreUltimate(C, g)
symbol_table.reader_meaning: A name that does not define the named by comparison to something deeper or larger.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A02: 'He cannot be defined by anything deeper or larger—He is the root, not a thing among things.'

symbol_table.formal_definition: A binary relation on entities: G(x, y) means x grounds or explains y.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: The relation of being more fundamental or explanatory.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A02: 'defined by anything deeper or larger'

symbol_table.formal_definition: A binary relation on categories: MoreUltimate(C, g) means category C is more ultimate than entity g.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: A category that would be more fundamental than the entity.

explicit_premises: There is a grounding relation G on entities.
There is a category membership relation and a MoreUltimate relation on categories and entities.
assumptions_and_dependencies.theological_starting_premises: The entity g is God, and the name N is 'I AM WHO I AM'.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There exists at least one entity g and name N such that RootNaming(N, g) holds, or the definition is vacuously true for all entities.

verification_controls.interpretation: Lean corpus not searched; no module compiled.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal definition of root-naming is proposed, capturing the logical structure of the claim that God is not defined by anything deeper or larger.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether the definition is non-vacuous, whether it corresponds to any existing Lean formalization, and whether the theological premises are consistent with the formal model.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The formalization abstracts away from the specific theological content and focuses on the relational structure. It does not capture the full meaning of 'I AM' as a divine name.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: This definition can be used as a building block for formalizing other claims about divine attributes and revelation.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: We can study the world to learn about God (discovery), and we can listen to what God says about Himself (disclosure). They are different, but they should fit together.
source_selection.reason: The claim asserts a convergence relation between two distinct epistemic sources: discovery (inference from the world) and disclosure (divine speech). This can be modeled as a compatibility or consistency condition between two sets of propositions.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: Let D be the set of propositions known by discovery and R be the set of propositions known by revelation. D and R are convergent if their union is consistent, i.e., there is no proposition p such that p ∈ D and ¬p ∈ R.

symbol_table.formal_definition: A set D of propositions obtained by reasoning from the world.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: Knowledge gained by studying the world.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A04: 'study the world to learn about God'

symbol_table.formal_definition: A set R of propositions obtained by divine revelation.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: Knowledge gained by listening to God's self-disclosure.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A04: 'listen to what God says about Himself'

symbol_table.formal_definition: D and R are convergent iff ¬∃p. p ∈ D ∧ ¬p ∈ R.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: The two sources do not contradict each other.

explicit_premises: There are two sets of propositions D and R.
Propositions can be negated and checked for membership.
assumptions_and_dependencies.theological_starting_premises: D is the set of truths about God discoverable by reason; R is the set of truths God has revealed.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There exist non-empty D and R that are convergent.

verification_controls.interpretation: Lean corpus not searched; no module compiled.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal definition of convergence between discovery and disclosure is proposed, capturing the idea that they should not contradict.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether the sets D and R are actually consistent, and whether this formalization captures the intended theological nuance.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The formalization reduces 'fitting together' to logical consistency, which may be too weak or too strong depending on interpretation.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: This definition can be used to formalize the claim that reason and revelation are compatible.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: Jesus doesn't just talk about God—He says things like 'I am the bread of life' and 'I am the truth,' using the same 'I am' language God used for Himself. That's identity language, not just religious advice.
source_selection.reason: The claim is about identity language: Jesus uses the same 'I am' formula as God in Exodus 3:14. This can be modeled as a relation between utterances and a shared predicate 'I am'.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: Let U be a set of utterances. An utterance u is an 'I am' utterance if it has the form 'I am X'. Two 'I am' utterances are identity-linked if they share the same subject 'I' and the same copula 'am'. Jesus's 'I am' sayings are identity-linked to God's 'I AM WHO I AM'.

symbol_table.formal_definition: An utterance of the form 'I am X'.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: A statement where the speaker identifies themselves with a predicate.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A03: 'I am the bread of life'

symbol_table.formal_definition: Two 'I am' utterances are identity-linked if they share the same subject and copula.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: They use the same self-identification formula.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A03: 'using the same 'I am' language God used for Himself'

explicit_premises: There is a set of utterances.
Utterances can be parsed into subject, copula, and predicate.
assumptions_and_dependencies.theological_starting_premises: God's utterance in Exodus 3:14 is 'I AM WHO I AM'; Jesus's utterances include 'I am the bread of life', etc.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There exist at least two 'I am' utterances that are identity-linked.

result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether this linguistic parallel implies identity of being, and whether the formalization captures the theological claim.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The formalization is purely syntactic and does not address semantic identity.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: This can be used to formalize arguments about Jesus's divine identity based on linguistic patterns.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: If Christianity is true, then what we find in the world, in logic, in history, and in our lives should fit with the God it describes.
source_selection.reason: This is a conditional prediction: if Christianity is true, then there is convergence between the world and the Christian description of God. This can be formalized as a conditional statement about consistency.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: If Christianity is true, then the set of propositions about the world (from reason, history, experience) is consistent with the set of propositions about God as described by Christianity.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: We can describe what Christianity says about God without first proving it. Then we can ask whether the world, our reasoning, history, and our experience line up with that description.
source_selection.reason: This claim is about the methodology of stating a hypothesis before testing it. It can be formalized as a two-step process: first define a description, then check consistency with evidence.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A 'disclosed portrait' is a set of propositions about God that can be stated without proof. A 'convergence test' is a procedure that checks whether the disclosed portrait is consistent with a set of evidential propositions.

symbol_table.formal_definition: A set P of propositions about God.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: The description of God Christianity offers.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A06: 'describe what Christianity says about God'

symbol_table.formal_definition: A function that takes P and a set E of evidential propositions and returns true if P ∪ E is consistent.
symbol_table.reader_meaning: Checking if the description lines up with evidence.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A06: 'ask whether the world, our reasoning, history, and our experience line up'

explicit_premises: There is a set P of propositions about God.
There is a set E of evidential propositions.
Consistency is defined as absence of contradiction.
assumptions_and_dependencies.theological_starting_premises: P is the Christian description of God.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There exists a non-empty P and E such that the convergence test returns true.
